clue.text: Rates about girls

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about charges levied on young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rates' is a verb here: to class someone is to rate them.
explanation.definitionFit: To rank or grade things is to rate them, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Room cleaner receiving a medal

indicators.note: the first word takes the following letters into itself

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady in British usage
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is an honour with a medal

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is awarded an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal or private apartment, an old synonym for a room.

clue.text: Unlooked-for snowfall can be a disaster!

definitions.text: Unlooked-for snowfall can be a disaster!

parts.words: Unlooked-for snowfall can be a disaster!
parts.note: an unexpected heavy fall of snow, here one sliding down a mountainside

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden mass of snow rushing down a slope, often deadly.

clue.text: Bag about fifty-it's easy

indicators.note: the first word goes about the second

parts.note: a sack is a bag
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Carrying a bag around fifty is no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose and undemanding, a period of light effort.

clue.text: A Persian ruler some like in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are read from the end

parts.note: part means some of something
as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: A Persian monarch whom some people admire looking back.
explanation.definitionFit: A provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: Old poetry that's among the crassest in all respects

indicators.note: the letters sit among the following words, running across their joins

explanation.surface: A critic damning some antique verse as the crudest work in every way.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict six-stanza verse form from the troubadours of medieval Provence, so a kind of old poem.

clue.text: The odd vet's idea for giving a tranquilliser

indicators.note: odd suggests these letters are strangely arranged

parts.note: the possessive keeps its S as a letter

explanation.surface: A strange notion from a veterinary surgeon about calming drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A calming drug, a synonym.

clue.text: Foreigners' resorts to hold back tax

definitions.note: the plural possessive: the answer names the people, with the 's as a link

indicators.note: the outer word holds the other within it

parts.note: spas are health resorts

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to drain is to tax or exhaust

explanation.surface: Overseas visitors' holiday spots evading duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Spain, foreigners to a British setter.

clue.text: Providing cover — how sweet!

definitions.meaning: coating a cake with frosting covers it
the sugary topping is the sweet part

explanation.definitionFit: Frosting a cake covers it, and the sugary coating is sweet.

clue.text: Man painting egghead entertainer

parts.note: an artist is someone who paints
the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: An intellectual painter turned stage performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but here it is the head of egg, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Getting mad at an inflexible arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone losing their temper over a rigid scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unyielding in opinion is firmly resolved, a direct synonym.

clue.text: An everyday sort of writer

parts.note: seems to mean an ordinary, unremarkable author, but describes someone who writes something each and every day

explanation.definitionFit: A journal keeper records events daily, so writes every day.

clue.text: Not reaching a target, they may be fired

definitions.text: Not reaching a target, they may be fired

parts.words: Not reaching a target, they may be fired
parts.note: sounds like failing workers facing dismissal, but describes rounds with no bullet that are shot yet hit nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Rounds loaded with powder but no bullet are discharged without striking anything.

clue.text: Brazilian port is seen everywhere around the City

indicators.note: the first word's letters go around the second's

parts.note: something rife is widespread, found all over
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A Brazilian harbour town is said to be overrun with urban life.
explanation.definitionFit: A major port city in north-east Brazil, capital of Pernambuco state.

clue.text: At the bottom of the river?

definitions.text: At the bottom of the river?

parts.words: At the bottom of the river?
parts.note: a flower, read as something that flows, is a river, and a bed is the bottom of one, while the real sense is a garden plot

explanation.definitionFit: A garden plot of soil where blooms are grown.

clue.text: Topping basic wear!

parts.note: reads as praise for splendid simple clothes, but describes something worn over the top of footwear

explanation.definitionFit: A galosh is a protective covering pulled on over ordinary footwear.

clue.text: Fear there could be loose parts-without attachment

indicators.note: loose letters are free to fall into another order

explanation.surface: Worry that some components may come apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Not in love, uncommitted emotionally.

clue.text: Such language is used by people at the bar!

definitions.text: Such language is used by people at the bar!

parts.words: Such language is used by people at the bar!
parts.note: suggests pub talk among drinkers, but the bar is the legal profession and its jargon

explanation.definitionFit: Jargon of lawyers, full of technical terms.

clue.text: Indians make coke here

indicators.note: make signals that these letters are made into something else

explanation.surface: Native Americans producing a fuel or drink on this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people originally of the south-eastern United States, once called Indians.

clue.text: The case for getting top politicians together

definitions.meaning: a cupboard or display case with shelves
the senior ministers of a government as a body

explanation.definitionFit: Both a piece of storage furniture and a body of senior ministers.

clue.text: Doubtfully interrogate a social worker

parts.note: to interrogate is to ask questions
an ant is a worker in an insect colony, a social creature

explanation.surface: Questioning a care worker sceptically.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking sideways or with suspicion, an old adverb for distrustfully.

clue.text: To let a large number in can cause distress

indicators.note: the letters for the number go in the other word

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A landlord letting to a crowd may cause anguish.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe suffering or anguish, a synonym.

clue.text: Coming changes to end VAT

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new word

explanation.surface: A forthcoming reform to scrap a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival, the season of the coming of Christ.

clue.text: Speculators becoming increasingly superior?

parts.note: punters who place wagers are those who bet, and if they keep improving the phrase for growing ever finer fits them doubly

explanation.definitionFit: Ever improving, steadily more excellent, the idiom for progressive improvement.

clue.text: Object over the charge

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: it can stand for any object

explanation.surface: Disputing a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy of one tenth paid to the church.

clue.text: She's written a couple of letters

parts.note: the letter L written out as a word
the letter N written out as a word

explanation.surface: A woman has penned two short notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written' tells you the two letters, L and N, are spelt out as words.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name.

clue.text: Weighty communication cut by a lawyer

indicators.note: the first word is split open by the following letters

parts.note: a note is a brief written message
BL is a Bachelor of Law

explanation.surface: An important letter abridged by a solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something important or worth noting carries weight, a synonym.

clue.text: The new general's swell!

indicators.note: a new version of the word has its letters reshuffled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine newly appointed military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like the slang adjective for great, but it is the verb meaning grow larger.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand or make bigger, as a tissue does when it puffs up.

clue.text: A down-trodden machine operator

parts.note: suggests an oppressed factory hand, but describes a foot lever literally trodden down to drive a machine

explanation.definitionFit: A foot pedal that powers a sewing machine or lathe when pressed repeatedly.

clue.text: Brown, a little gentleman, won't cross the line

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
gent is a shortened form of gentleman

explanation.surface: A suntanned gent who refuses to step over a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't cross the' is a gloss: this line touches a curve without crossing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight geometric ray that touches a curve at one point without cutting it.
